question.problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}({e}^{x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(2{e}^{x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}({e}^{2x})\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
question.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{x} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})={e}^{x} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})={e}^{x} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})={e}^{x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $A$ contains only one element:

$$
A={{e}^{x}}
$$

Consequently, $|A|=1,$ which is finite.

- The set $B$ is finite. Similar to the previous case, $B$ contains only one element:

$$
A={2{e}^{x}}.
$$

Consequently, $|B|=1,$ which is finite.

- The set $C$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{2x} \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{2x})=2{e}^{2x} \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{2x})=4{e}^{2x} \\ {h}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{2x})=8{e}^{2x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
C={{e}^{2x},2{e}^{2x},4{e}^{2x},8{e}^{2x},…}
$$

Consequently, $C$ is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$C$ only."

choices.value: None of the sets are infinite.

responses.value: None of the sets are infinite.
